I will keep my farm simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the crop I trust most is the winter wheat and summer maize rotation, because I know it fits the land, the weather, and the water conditions, and it gives me grain from the same fields in two seasons. At my age, I would not spread myself across many complicated crops that need constant watching or too much hired labor. I would put most of my land into wheat followed by maize, and I would keep a small piece for spring peanuts to bring in some cash and spread risk a little. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and reduces trouble, keep fertilizer moderate instead of excessive, irrigate only at the important stages, and use pesticide only when I need to protect the crop. For tillage, I would choose the methods that save labor and let me finish field work on time.
